sentences.text: Teviornis holds the distinction of being the oldest known neognath bird, a group that includes all modern birds, alongside the species Vegavis.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a crushed partial right forelimb.
This ancient bird lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
Its genus name combines the Greek word for bird with the name of Victor Tereschenko, the paleontologist who discovered the specimen.
Fossils were collected from the Nemegt Formation at the Guriliin Tsav locality in the northwest corner of Umnogobi Aimak, Mongolia.
The catalog number for the holotype fossils is PIN 4499–1, and they are housed in the collection of the Paleontological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow.
The species name T. gobiensis refers to the Gobi Desert where the fossil was discovered.
The fossil site where Teviornis was found also yielded remains of Tarbosaurus, Gallimimus, Oksoko, Saurolophus, Prenocephale, and Gurilynia.
The same locality also contained fossils of the turtle Mongolochelys, an azhdarchid pterosaur, and a metatherian mammal.
Teviornis was originally described in 2002 by Kurochkin, Dyke, and Karhu as a member of the family Presbyornithidae.
If Teviornis belongs to Presbyornithidae, it suggests that relatives of modern waterfowl were widespread and highly evolved by the end of the Mesozoic.
A 2016 study by De Pietri and colleagues confirmed Teviornis as a presbyornithid based on features like the trochlea carpalis extension.
A 2019 study supports the classification of presbyornithids as stem anseriforms.
The time range for Teviornis is estimated between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
Clarke and Norell (2004) argued that characters originally used to assign Teviornis to Anseriformes, like an unbowed metacarpal III, are primitive traits retained in other bird groups.
Recent phylogenetic analyses have produced conflicting results, with a 2023 study placing Teviornis as a presbyornithid and a 2025 study placing it as a basal ornithurine.
